title: Essential Transformations: map, batch, shuffle 📊
description: Learn the core dataset transformations to prepare data for training.

slides.title: Chaining Transformations ⛓️
slides.content:
# Datasets Are Lazy and Composable

Each transformation returns a **new Dataset** object. No computation happens until you iterate or call `.fit()`.

Common transformations:
- `.map(fn)` – apply a function to each element.
- `.batch(batch_size)` – group elements into batches.
- `.shuffle(buffer_size)` – randomly shuffle elements.
- `.repeat(count)` – repeat the dataset indefinitely or N times.
- `.prefetch(buffer_size)` – prepare next batch while current one is processed.

slides.title: A Typical Pipeline
slides.codeSnippet:
dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((X_train, y_train))
dataset = dataset.shuffle(buffer_size=1000)
dataset = dataset.batch(32)
dataset = dataset.map(preprocess_fn, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
dataset = dataset.prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

model.fit(dataset, epochs=5)

quizData.question: Why should `batch` usually come before `map` for heavy operations?

options.text: So the map function processes whole batches, enabling vectorised operations
To reduce the number of files

quizData.explanation: Mapping after batching applies the function to batches, which is often more efficient than per‑element.

slides.title: The `map` Function 🗺️
slides.content:
# Transform Each Element

- Takes a function that receives one element (or a tuple if multiple components).
- Returns the transformed element.
- Use `num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE` for parallel execution.

```python
def rescale(x, y):
    return x / 255.0, y

dataset = dataset.map(rescale, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
```

slides.title: Shuffle & Batch Mechanics
slides.content: Shuffle uses a buffer; it randomly picks elements from the buffer.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Shuffle: good buffer size ~ dataset size for perfect randomness (if memory allows)
dataset = dataset.shuffle(buffer_size=10000)

# Batch: groups consecutive elements
dataset = dataset.batch(32)

# Drop remainder if uneven last batch?
dataset = dataset.batch(32, drop_remainder=True)

slides.title: Shuffle Buffer Size 💡
slides.content: A buffer larger than your dataset gives uniform randomness. If memory is tight, use a fraction (e.g., 10%). Larger = better randomness but more RAM.
